• The “ribonucleoprotein particle” that recognizes a nascent polypeptide chain and tells it to “pause” is the signal-recognition particle (SRP).  
• SRP binds the emerging chain as it exits the ribosome in the cytosol, temporarily halting translation.  
• SRP then guides ( “let me show you in” ) the ribosome–nascent-chain complex to the rough endoplasmic reticulum (hence the chain’s comment that “it seems somewhat rough”).  
• Once inside the ER, the polypeptide immediately begins to receive N-linked glycosylation (“you really need some sugar”).  
• Proteins that enter the ER lumen continue through the secretory pathway (ER → Golgi → secretory vesicles) and are ultimately destined for the extracellular space.  

Thus, they first meet in the cytosol, and the chain’s ultimate journey is toward secretion outside the cell.

Answer: C
